The issue reported states that the state of the option groups is not updated by the default options during parsing. This means that when a command line argument specifies one option and the default options contain another mutually exclusive option, the parser does not complain and both options end up in the resulting CommandLine.

By examining the code snippet of the `parse` method in `org.apache.commons.cli.DefaultParser`, we can see that the method initializes the `OptionGroup` state but does not handle updating it based on the default options provided.

To resolve this issue, the `handleProperties` method in the `parse` function should update the state of the option groups based on the default options provided in the `properties`.

Next, I will provide the best locations to fix this bug.
The bug can be fixed in the following method:

`org.apache.commons.cli.DefaultParser.parse(org.apache.commons.cli.Options, java.lang.String[], java.util.Properties, boolean)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
